description: Summer HW Task 2: Terminologies related to biological bases of behavior (Psychology and Life Ch3).

words.definition: γ-氨基丁酸 (The primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain; undersupply linked to seizures, tremors, and anxiety)
words.example: Anti-anxiety medications like benzodiazepines enhance GABA receptor sensitivity to calm nervous activity.
words.mnemonic: GABA = Get A Break Already: brakes of the brain, puts a stop to runaway firing.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 去甲肾上腺素 (Neurotransmitter and hormone that helps control alertness and physical arousal; undersupply can depress mood)
words.example: Norepinephrine constricts blood vessels and sharpens concentration during stressful encounters.
words.mnemonic: No-Re-pining: keeps you alert and energized in danger.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 谷氨酸盐 (The primary excitatory neurotransmitter in the brain involved in memory; oversupply can overstimulate brain producing migraines or seizures)
words.example: Excess glutamate release following a stroke contributes to excitotoxicity and cellular death.
words.mnemonic: Glut-ton of Excitement: gluing memories together, excitatory!
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 内啡肽 (Natural, opiate-like neurotransmitters linked to pain alleviation and feelings of pleasure during exertion or injury)
words.example: The 'runner's high' is mediated by endogenous endorphin release in the central nervous system.
words.mnemonic: Endogenous Morphine: internal painkiller produced by the body.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 5-羟色胺 (Neurotransmitter affecting mood, hunger, sleep, and arousal; undersupply strongly linked to clinical depression)
words.example: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs) boost synaptic serotonin levels to relieve depressive symptoms.
words.mnemonic: Sir Rotten-mood needs Serotonin to feel bright and balanced.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 多巴胺 (Neurotransmitter influencing movement, learning, attention, and the brain's reward/pleasure circuits)
words.example: Excess dopamine activity is linked to schizophrenia, while dopamine neuron loss causes tremors in Parkinson's disease.
words.mnemonic: DOPE = makes you feel rewarded; Dopamine drives anticipation and reward.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 乙酰胆碱 (Neurotransmitter enabling muscle contraction, voluntary movement, attention, and memory; deteriorates in Alzheimer's disease)
words.example: Curare poison blocks acetylcholine receptors, resulting in paralysis, while botulinum toxin prevents its release.
words.mnemonic: ACh = Action & Memory: activates muscles and memory.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 神经递质 (Chemical messengers released across the synaptic cleft that bind to receptor sites on receiving neurons)
words.example: Dopamine and serotonin are crucial neurotransmitters influencing human affect and motivation.
words.mnemonic: Keys fitting into specific lock receptors on the receiving cell.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 神经冲动 (An action potential; a brief electrical charge that travels down an axon generated by the movement of positively charged ions)
words.example: A neural impulse operates on an all-or-none principle: it fires completely or not at all.
words.mnemonic: The spark of electricity rushing down the axon wire.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 神经传导 (The electrochemical process by which signaling molecules are released by axon terminals to bind to receptors on adjacent cells)
words.example: Psychoactive medications act primarily by altering steps in synaptic neurotransmission.
words.mnemonic: Sending electrical and chemical signals across the synapse.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neurotransmission

words.definition: 神经 (Bundled cables formed by many axons connecting the central nervous system with muscles, glands, and sensory organs)
words.example: The optic nerve carries over a million axon fibers from the retina to the thalamus.
words.mnemonic: Heavy multi-strand cables carrying biological data.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neuron

words.definition: 突触 (The microscopic junction between the axon terminal of the sending neuron and the dendrite or cell body of the receiving neuron)
words.example: Neurotransmitters diffuse across the synaptic gap in less than a millisecond.
words.mnemonic: The tiny gap where neurons snap/chat with chemicals.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neuron

words.definition: 髓鞘 (Layer of fatty tissue encasing the axon that dramatically speeds up neural impulse transmission via saltatory conduction)
words.example: Multiple sclerosis results from the progressive degeneration of the myelin sheath, causing communication breakdown.
words.mnemonic: Plastic insulation around an electrical cord; speeds up the signal.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neuron

words.definition: 胞体 (The metabolic life-support center of a neuron containing the nucleus and sustaining cell health)
words.example: The soma integrates incoming electrical potentials from all dendrites before firing.
words.mnemonic: Soma = body: the core body keeping the neuron alive.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neuron

words.definition: 轴突 (Long fiber of a neuron through which neural electrical impulses pass to terminal branches to communicate with other cells)
words.example: Some motor axons extend over a meter from the lower spine down to the muscles in the foot.
words.mnemonic: Axon = Away: sends messages Away from the cell body.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neuron

words.definition: 树突 (Bushy, branching extensions of a neuron that receive chemical messages and conduct impulses toward the cell body)
words.example: Dendrites possess numerous synaptic receptors where neurotransmitters bind.
words.mnemonic: Dendrites Deliver: tree branches reaching out to listen to neighbors.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neuron

words.definition: 神经元 (A nerve cell; the fundamental building block of the nervous system specialized for electrochemical signaling)
words.example: Each sensory neuron transmits environmental impulses toward the spinal cord and brain.
words.mnemonic: The single micro-transistor and communicator of the brain.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Neuron

words.definition: 胼胝体 (The wide band of axon fibers connecting the left and right cerebral hemispheres, facilitating interhemispheric communication)
words.example: In split-brain surgery, the corpus callosum is severed to prevent severe epileptic seizures from spreading.
words.mnemonic: Corpus Call-Someone: the phone cable calling between left and right hemispheres.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 大脑半球 (The left and right symmetrical halves of the cerebrum, each specialized for distinct cognitive functions)
words.example: In most people, the left cerebral hemisphere is specialized for language, while the right handles spatial perception.
words.mnemonic: Half of the spherical cerebrum.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 颞叶 (Cortex region above the ears containing auditory cortex and Wernicke's area; processes hearing, speech comprehension, and face recognition)
words.example: The primary auditory cortex in the temporal lobes decodes musical pitch and speech sounds.
words.mnemonic: Near your temples and ears: Tempo (music/hearing) and Tone.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 枕叶 (Cortex region at the back of head containing visual cortex; processes visual information)
words.example: A blow to the occipital lobes can cause temporary blindness or seeing stars.
words.mnemonic: Occipital = Optical / Octopus with eyes on the back of its head.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 顶叶 (Cortex region at top-rear of head containing somatosensory cortex; processes touch, body position, and spatial orientation)
words.example: The somatosensory strip in the parietal lobes registers sensations of warmth, pressure, and pain.
words.mnemonic: Parietal = Piranha bites you on the top of the head; you feel the touch and bite.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 额叶 (Portion of cerebral cortex behind forehead involved in speaking, muscle movement, planning, judgement, and impulse control)
words.example: Phineas Gage suffered damage to his frontal lobes, dramatically altering his personality and social restraint.
words.mnemonic: At the front of your head: the CEO of the brain, making plans and decisions.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 大脑皮层 (The intricate, wrinkled outer layer of gray matter covering cerebral hemispheres; the body's ultimate control and information-processing center)
words.example: The convoluted folding of the cerebral cortex dramatically increases its surface area inside the cranium.
words.mnemonic: Cortex = bark of a tree: the wrinkled outer bark of the brain.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 大脑 (The largest part of the human brain comprising two cerebral hemispheres responsible for thought, language, and perception)
words.example: The cerebrum enables complex decision making, creative reasoning, and conscious experience.
words.mnemonic: Cerebrum = the big thinking brain.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 海马 (Curved neural structure in limbic system essential for consolidating new explicit memories into long-term storage)
words.example: Patient H.M. lost his hippocampus and could no longer form new episodic memories, while retaining older ones.
words.mnemonic: Hippo on campus: if you saw a hippo walking on your campus, you would definitely remember it!
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain, Limbic system

words.definition: 杏仁核 (Two almond-shaped neural clusters in the limbic system linked to emotional processing, particularly fear and aggression)
words.example: Damage to the amygdala in monkeys produces Kluver-Bucy syndrome, characterized by a lack of fear.
words.mnemonic: Amygdala sounds like 'Amy G. Dala' — a scary monster triggering panic and anger; almond-shaped.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain, Limbic system

words.definition: 边缘系统 (Neural system located below cerebral hemispheres associated with emotions, drives, and memory; includes amygdala, hippocampus, hypothalamus)
words.example: The limbic system bridges primitive brainstem reflexes with advanced cortical deliberation.
words.mnemonic: Hungry, angry, emotional, and remembering: HAH (Hippocampus, Amygdala, Hypothalamus).
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain, Limbic system

words.definition: 小脑 (The 'little brain' at the rear of brainstem; processes sensory input, coordinates balance, posture, and procedural motor memory)
words.example: Alcohol consumption impairs cerebellum function, resulting in slurred speech and loss of equilibrium.
words.mnemonic: Cere-BELL-um: like a ballerina balancing on a tightrope; bell ringer balance.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 丘脑 (The brain's sensory switchboard atop the brainstem; directs all incoming sensory signals except smell to the cortex)
words.example: Visual signals from the retina pass through the lateral geniculate nucleus of the thalamus before reaching the occipital lobe.
words.mnemonic: Hal & Amos: traffic cops directing all sensory traffic (except smell!).
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 间脑 (Forebrain division between cerebrum and midbrain containing the thalamus and hypothalamus)
words.example: The diencephalon acts as the primary relay and endocrine regulation center of the central nervous system.
words.mnemonic: Di = two (Thalamus and Hypothalamus).
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 网状结构 (Nerve network traveling through brainstem that plays a central role in controlling alertness and arousal)
words.example: If the reticular formation is severed, an animal lapses into an irreversible coma.
words.mnemonic: Re-Tickle-ar: tickle me awake; controls arousal and waking up.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 中脑 (Segment of brainstem between pons and diencephalon integrating sensory information with motor output and dopamine production)
words.example: The substantia nigra in the midbrain produces dopamine crucial for smooth voluntary movement.
words.mnemonic: In the middle of the brainstem, routing visual and auditory orientation reflexes.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 脑桥 (Structure above medulla that acts as a bridge coordinating movement, facial expressions, and sleep/dream states)
words.example: The pons contains nuclei that initiate REM sleep and suppress muscle activity during dreaming.
words.mnemonic: Pons = French for bridge (pont) / pond: relax near the pond for sleep, dreams, and coordination.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 延髓 (Base of brainstem controlling heartbeat, respiration, swallowing, and vomiting reflexes)
words.example: The medulla keeps you breathing automatically even when in deep unconscious sleep.
words.mnemonic: Med-medal: wearing a medal over your heart and lungs (controls heartbeat & breathing).
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 脑干 (Oldest evolutionary brain region; controls automatic survival functions like breathing, heartbeat, and blood pressure)
words.example: Damage to the brainstem is often fatal because it regulates involuntary vital functions.
words.mnemonic: The stem that holds up the flower; without the stem, the whole brain dies.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Brain

words.definition: 副交感神经系统 (Division of ANS that calms the body to conserve energy; the rest-and-digest system)
words.example: After the danger passes, the parasympathetic nervous system slows heart rate and stimulates digestion.
words.mnemonic: Para-parachute / Peace: restores peace, Rest & Digest.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Nervous system

words.definition: 交感神经系统 (Division of ANS that mobilizes energy in stressful situations; the fight-or-flight system)
words.example: When you encounter a snake on a trail, your sympathetic nervous system accelerates your heart and dilates pupils.
words.mnemonic: Has 'sympathy' for you when you are in danger: powers up Fight or Flight!
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Nervous system

words.definition: 自主神经系统 (Subdivision of PNS regulating involuntary vegetative processes: glands, heart rate, digestion)
words.example: The ANS maintains homeostasis automatically, regulating heartbeat and pupil dilation without conscious effort.
words.mnemonic: Automatic / Autonomic: operates on autopilot.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Nervous system

words.definition: 躯体神经系统 (Subdivision of PNS controlling voluntary movements of skeletal muscles and relaying sensory input)
words.example: Deciding to wave your hand relies on motor neurons in the somatic nervous system.
words.mnemonic: Soma = body; voluntary bodily muscle actions.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Nervous system

words.definition: 外周神经系统 (Sensory and motor neurons connecting the central nervous system to the rest of the body)
words.example: The PNS branches outward into somatic and autonomic systems.
words.mnemonic: Peripheral = on the outer edge, reaching hands, feet, and internal organs.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Nervous system

words.definition: 脊髓 (Thick column of neural tissue connecting brain to peripheral nerves and mediating simple reflexes)
words.example: The knee-jerk reflex is mediated directly by interneurons in the spinal cord without brain intervention.
words.mnemonic: The information highway running down the spine.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Nervous system

words.definition: 脑 (The primary organ of the central nervous system coordinating thought, emotion, sensory perception, and action)
words.example: The brain contains approximately 86 billion neurons communicating through trillions of synapses.
words.mnemonic: The supreme master computer of mind and behavior.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Nervous system, Brain

words.definition: 中枢神经系统 (The core decision-making division of the nervous system consisting of the brain and spinal cord)
words.example: The CNS coordinates high-level cognitive processes, sensory perception, and motor coordination.
words.mnemonic: Central command center: Head (brain) and Backbone (spinal cord).
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Nervous system

words.definition: 神经系统 (The body's speedy, electrochemical communication network comprising all nerve cells)
words.example: The nervous system processes sensory information and transmits motor commands in milliseconds.
words.mnemonic: The electrical wiring grid of the human body.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Nervous system

words.definition: 褪黑激素 (Pineal hormone regulating sleep-wake circadian cycles; rises in darkness, drops in light)
words.example: Exposure to blue screen light before bedtime suppresses melatonin, causing insomnia.
words.mnemonic: Mellow-tonin makes you mellow and sleepy when the lights go down.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system

words.definition: 松果体 (Small endocrine gland in the brain producing melatonin to modulate sleep-wake circadian cycles)
words.example: The pineal gland responds to darkness by increasing melatonin synthesis.
words.mnemonic: Pinecone-shaped gland in the center of the brain controlling night sleep.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system

words.definition: 催产素 (Pituitary hormone facilitating social bonding, maternal attachment, empathy, and uterine contractions)
words.example: Oxytocin, often called the 'cuddle hormone', promotes trust between mother and infant during nursing.
words.mnemonic: Oxy-TOC-in: Touch, Oxy, Caring — the love and social bonding hormone.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system

words.definition: 睾酮 (Primary male sex hormone produced in testes and adrenals stimulating male sexual traits and aggression)
words.example: Higher levels of testosterone have been correlated with risk-taking and competitive behavior.
words.mnemonic: Testes -> testosterone.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system

words.definition: 肾上腺素 (Hormone secreted by adrenal medulla that increases cardiac output and raises glucose levels in emergencies)
words.example: The sight of the oncoming truck triggered an adrenaline rush, preparing her to jump out of the way.
words.mnemonic: Epi (above) + nephros (kidney) -> adrenaline powers the fight-or-flight burst.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system

words.definition: 肾上腺 (Pair of endocrine glands situated above kidneys that secrete epinephrine and norepinephrine in stress)
words.example: During a flight-or-fight emergency, the adrenal glands release adrenaline to surge blood sugar and heart rate.
words.mnemonic: Ad-renal: adjacent to the renal (kidneys).
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system

words.definition: 生长激素 (Anterior pituitary hormone that stimulates somatic growth and cellular reproduction)
words.example: An oversecretion of growth hormone during childhood causes gigantism, while undersecretion causes dwarfism.
words.mnemonic: GH directly fuels physical Growth and Height.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system

words.definition: 垂体 (The endocrine system's master gland that under hypothalamus control regulates growth and other glands)
words.example: The pituitary gland secretes growth hormone and triggers puberty.
words.mnemonic: Pit boss / master of all endocrine glands.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system

words.definition: 下丘脑 (Brain structure below thalamus governing maintenance activities: the 4 F's — fighting, fleeing, feeding, and mating)
words.example: The hypothalamus signals the pituitary gland to trigger endocrine responses during stress.
words.mnemonic: Hypo (below) the thalamus; controls the 4 Fs: Feeding, Fleeing, Fighting, and Fornicating.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system, Limbic system

words.definition: 激素 (Chemical messengers manufactured by endocrine glands that travel through the bloodstream)
words.example: Hormones regulate physiological processes including hunger, sleep, mood, and reproduction.
words.mnemonic: Hormones rush into the blood to set the body in motion.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system

words.definition: 内分泌系统 (Glandular communication network that secretes hormones directly into the bloodstream)
words.example: The endocrine system works alongside the nervous system to coordinate metabolism, growth, and stress responses.
words.mnemonic: Endo = internal; secretes hormones inside the bloodstream slowly like radio broadcasts.
words.tags: AP Psychology, Ch3 Biological Bases, Endocrine system
